title: Blondie
paragraphs: Preservation subset of the 1939-1950 radio sitcom adapted from Chic Young’s comic strip. The frozen container also includes one Abbott & Costello guest broadcast and one promotional track, plus alternate AFRS/collection transfers; these are separated from the regular Blondie chronology.

GRH documents the program through CBS / Camel era (July 3, 1939 to June 26, 1944) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Blue Network / Super Suds summer run (July 21, 1944 to September 1, 1944) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], CBS / Super Suds era (August 13, 1944 to September 26, 1948) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and NBC / Super Suds era (October 6, 1948 to June 29, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Arthur Lake (performer on 41 recordings), Penny Singleton (performer on 29 recordings), Chic Young (creator on 18 recordings), Hanley Stafford (performer on 15 recordings), Bill Goodwin (announcer on 7 recordings), Billy Artz (conductor on 6 recordings), and Lenny Conn and His Orchestra (performer on 5 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family and domestic comedy, marriage and household mishaps, children and family life, workplace comedy and Mr. Dithers, holiday and seasonal comedy, and celebrity guest and cross-series comedy.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Comic strip characters move into film and radio, Sponsor and network transitions in commercial radio, AFRS reuse and preservation, and Domestic situation comedy in network radio.

GRH documents the program through CBS / Camel era (July 3, 1939 to June 26, 1944) on CBS Radio Network, Blue Network / Super Suds summer run (July 21, 1944 to September 1, 1944) on Blue Network, CBS / Super Suds era (August 13, 1944 to September 26, 1948) on CBS Radio Network, and NBC / Super Suds era (October 6, 1948 to June 29, 1949) on NBC Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Arthur Lake (performer on 41 recordings), Penny Singleton (performer on 29 recordings), Chic Young (creator on 18 recordings), Hanley Stafford (performer on 15 recordings), Bill Goodwin (announcer on 7 recordings), Billy Artz (conductor on 6 recordings), and Lenny Conn and His Orchestra (performer on 5 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to CBS Radio Network (broadcast on network), Armed Forces Radio Service (rebroadcast by), and NBC Radio Network (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family and domestic comedy, marriage and household mishaps, children and family life, workplace comedy and Mr. Dithers, holiday and seasonal comedy, and celebrity guest and cross-series comedy.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Comic strip characters move into film and radio, Sponsor and network transitions in commercial radio, AFRS reuse and preservation, and Domestic situation comedy in network radio.
